title: How much to cook, and how to run production day

say: How much to cook, and how to run production day.
This is the video for module two of Catering Basics and Food Safety: menus, portions and production day.
A good event menu is a set of dishes that suit the guests, survive the journey and stay safe for hours.

say: First, ask the serving time, format, guest numbers, budget and any allergies. Then plan one plate: a starch, a protein, a side, and sometimes an extra. Choose dishes that hold well in a hot cooler, like jollof rice, stews, moi moi and well-cooked meats.

panel.heading: Dishes that hold, dishes that don't

say: Fried plantain softens, salad wilts once dressed, and pounded yam forms a skin. Plan these for last-minute work, or swap them out. Halima dropped fried plantain from a wedding menu because it would be soft after a 3-hour hold.

panel.heading: Dishes that hold, dishes that don't

say: Step one. Test your portion. Cook a measured amount of raw rice, serve it with your usual spoon into your usual pack, and count the packs. Your spoon and your pack decide your number.

panel.heading: From guest count to shopping list

say: Step two. Multiply each portion by the number of guests.

panel.heading: From guest count to shopping list
items: Test your portion with your own spoon
Multiply by the number of guests

say: Step three. Add a buffer, usually around 10 percent, because guest numbers grow and servers give bigger spoons.

panel.heading: From guest count to shopping list
items: Test your portion with your own spoon
Multiply by the number of guests

say: Step four. Turn totals into what you actually buy: kilograms of rice, whole birds, crates of eggs, litres of oil.

panel.rule: Portion × guests + about 10% buffer = total quantity

say: Ngozi tested her portions: 120 grams of raw rice and one chicken piece per adult. For 100 guests, that is 12 kilograms of rice.
She adds 10%, which gives 13.2 kilograms, so she buys 14.
For chicken, 100 pieces plus 10% is 110. She cuts each bird into 8 pieces, and 110 divided by 8 is 13.75, so she buys 14 birds.
Coleslaw is 80 grams each, so 8 kilograms plus 10%, about 8.8 kilograms.
To scale a recipe, divide the new servings by the old. From 10 servings to 50, the factor is 5. Season gradually and taste, and never cram a pot beyond its size.

Ronke caters 100 packs for a 1:00 pm church anniversary, 45 minutes away. She works backwards from serving time. The day before, she steams moi moi and cools it fast, makes the stew base and refrigerates it, and shreds the cabbage.

panel.heading: Ronke's 100-pack timetable
items: Day before: moi moi, stew base, cut cabbage

say: At 6:30 am, she boils chicken, starts the first batch of rice, and heats the stew base to boiling.

panel.heading: Ronke's 100-pack timetable
items: Day before: moi moi, stew base, cut cabbage

say: By 10:00 am everything is cooked. She probe-checks the chicken at 70 degrees or above and the rice above 60.

panel.heading: Ronke's 100-pack timetable
items: Day before: moi moi, stew base, cut cabbage

say: She packs hot food into coolers preheated with hot water for 10 minutes, and coleslaw into a separate cooler with ice packs.

panel.heading: Ronke's 100-pack timetable
items: Day before: moi moi, stew base, cut cabbage

say: She leaves at 11:00 am and arrives at 11:45, with 75 minutes of buffer before serving.

panel.rule: Work backwards from serving time. Buffers are not wasted time.

say: Set up a raw zone, with its own table, board, knife and bin for raw chicken, meat and fish.

say: Keep gas cylinders upright, outside or in a well-ventilated space, away from the flame.

cards.d: Keep LPG cylinders upright, outside or well ventilated, away from the flame.

say: To remember. Plan one plate, then multiply. Portion times guests, plus about 10%. Build your timetable backwards with buffers. Keep three zones. And preheat your coolers, with cold food in its own cooler.

Now practise. Write two menu packages with holding notes. Build a quantity sheet for 50 and 100 guests. Plan a production day working back from a 1:00 pm serving, and sketch your kitchen zones with an equipment checklist.
